podcast.title: Banalization of Words
podcast.body: Ni Ganswizatitude played an active role in the banalization of two significant words: "nigga" and "bitch." The trivialization of "nigga," despite its consistently negative historical connotations, is suggested to have possibly originated from their song "niga niga." The word "bitch" was used with such extensive frequency in their second album, "nigas por life," that the band is likely a primary contributor to its widespread, casual usage. "Nigas Wizzatitude participaron activamente en la banalización de todos grandes palabras, por un lado la palabra niga, aunque la palabra niga siempre se ha usado con connotaciones muy negativas, posiblemente la banalización de la palabra niga venga, de la canción niga niga, de los nigas Wizzatitude, y la segunda es la banalización de la palabra pitch, o sea la palabra pitch en el segundo álbum de niga Wizzatitude sale tantas veces que posiblemente sean los protagonistas y culpables."

podcast.title: Band Formation and Instability
podcast.body: Ni Ganswizatitude was characterized as a highly unstable band that never truly achieved cohesion, primarily due to poor relationships among its members. Their formation in the mid-80s was driven by necessity, as many rappers were vying for attention in the fervent and extensive Afro-American hip hop scene. Group formation was a common strategy for artists to stand out and increase their collective strength. "Los miembros de Ni Ganswizatitude se juntaron un poco por necesidad porque de aquella es bueno, a mitad de los 80, cuando empiezan a trabajar ellos, había un montón de raperos intentando destacarles."

podcast.title: Ephemeral Myth and Suburban Pride
podcast.body: Ni Ganswizatitude achieved a mythical status, though it was an ephemeral one given the band's relatively short lifespan. They championed a philosophy of pride associated with belonging to suburbs that were characterized by illegal, macabre, or otherwise questionable attitudes, effectively transforming this affiliation into a matter of honor and self-respect. "Ellos se convirtieron en un mito, aunque un mito tanto fímero porque la banda duraría poco tiempo, y empezaron esa filosofía de sentirse orgullosos, don suburbio lleno de actitudes ilegales o de actitudes macabras o de actitudes cuestionables."

podcast.title: Gangsta Rap Pioneers
podcast.body: Ni Ganswizatitude is widely considered the absolute fathers of the "gangster movement" and "gangster rap," which emerged in the late 1980s. While there's a debate about whether they were the very first, they are unequivocally recognized as the progenitors of "hardcore gangsta rap." They effectively broke a generational gap, establishing themselves as the absolute leaders of this movement and marking a significant "before and after" in the timeline of rap lyrics. "Si nos queremos ir a los orígenes de todo esto, muy posiblemente nos tengamos que ir a Ni Ganswizatitude, padres absolutos, el movimiento gangster, del gangster rap que nace a finales de los 80."

podcast.title: Post-Album Controversies and Dissolution
podcast.body: Immediately after the release of their first album, Ni Ganswizatitude encountered substantial problems, including scrutiny from the FBI and organized campaigns by Republican politicians who vocally opposed the album's message, characteristic of controversial works. Internally, the band suffered severe disputes over financial rights, particularly concerning the main lyricists' compensation, which ultimately led to Sirren's departure. The band eventually dissolved after their second album due to these unresolved internal conflicts and significant questioning from within the Afro-American community regarding their controversial lyrical content. "Justo después de este disco, bueno, tuvieron un montón de problemas desde el FBI que entonces juraron el disco movimiento, es político republicano, en políticos que hicieron campaña contra el disco, bueno, estas peleas que siempre hay cuando algo es polémico."
